Add Census Socioeconomic variables to Health Data

Source: R/sus_socio_add_census.R
sus_census_join.Rd

Enriches spatialized health data with Brazilian Census variables from the censobr package, aggregated to municipality level (or joined by census tract). Run it after sus_spatial_join() (stage "spatial" or later) and before sus_socio_compute_indicators() and the epidemiological models. Use sus_census_select() to discover valid census_vars.

Usage

sus_census_join(
  df,
  dataset = "population",
  tracts_dataset = "Basico",
  year = 2010,
  census_vars = NULL,
  aggregation_fun = "sum",
  join_muni_col = NULL,
  join_level = c("muni", "tract"),
  join_tract_col = NULL,
  use_cache = TRUE,
  cache_dir = "~/.climasus4r_cache/census",
  lang = "pt",
  translate_columns = TRUE,
  standardize_values = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

A climasus_df (typically an sf from sus_spatial_join()) at stage "spatial" or later, containing code_muni_7 for the municipality join. Plain data.frame/sf objects that are not climasus_df error, except when join_level = "tract" (they are promoted). Non-data-frame input errors.

dataset

Character scalar, one of:

  • "population" (default) - population microdata

  • "households" - household microdata

  • "families" - family microdata

  • "mortality" - mortality microdata

  • "emigration" - emigration microdata

  • "tracts" - census-tract aggregates (setores censitarios); select the table with tracts_dataset. With join_level = "muni" the tract table is aggregated to municipality; with join_level = "tract" it is joined by tract code without aggregation.

Other values error.

tracts_dataset

Character scalar, used only when dataset = "tracts" (default "Basico"); validated by censobr::read_tracts(). Census 2010: "Basico", "Domicilio01", "Domicilio02", "DomicilioRenda", "Pessoa01" to "Pessoa13", "ResponsavelRenda", "ResponsavelRendaSexo". Census 2022: "Basico", "Pessoas", "Domicilio", "ResponsavelRenda", "Entorno", "Indigenas", "Quilombolas". See censobr::read_tracts() for the variables of each table.

year

Numeric scalar census year, default 2010; typical values 2000, 2010 or 2022 (a single year only, ranges/vectors are not supported). It is passed to censobr, which validates availability per dataset (2022 mainly for tracts).

census_vars

Character vector of census variable names to add, e.g. c("V0001", "V0002") (find them with sus_census_select()). Names not present in the table are silently ignored. NULL (default) keeps all variables (not recommended for microdata: heavy).

aggregation_fun

Character scalar used for join_level = "muni" to aggregate each numeric variable by municipality (NAs removed): "sum" (default; counts such as population), "mean" (e.g. income), "median", "min", "max", "sd", "q25", "q75", "q95", "q99". Other values error. Ignored for join_level = "tract".

join_muni_col

Character scalar or NULL. Intended name of the municipality-code column of df; currently NOT used (the join relies on code_muni_7, see Details). Default NULL.

join_level

Character scalar, "muni" (default) or "tract" (validated with match.arg()). "muni": aggregate to municipality and join by municipality code. "tract": only valid with dataset = "tracts" (otherwise errors); df is a table of tracts and the censobr table is joined by tract code.

join_tract_col

Character scalar or NULL. Column of df with the 15-digit tract code, used when join_level = "tract". NULL (default) auto-detects code_tract or CD_SETOR; a name not in df errors.

use_cache

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), sets the censobr cache directory to cache_dir so downloads are reused.

cache_dir

Character scalar. Cache directory, default "~/.climasus4r_cache/census"; created if missing and passed to censobr::set_censobr_cache_dir().

lang

Character scalar. Message (and column-translation) language: "pt" (default), "en" or "es"; other values fall back to "pt" with a warning.

translate_columns

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), translates census column names (municipality join only) to lang.

standardize_values

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), standardizes categorical values of the census table to lang (municipality join only).

verbose

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages and a download progress bar.

Value

The input object (sf geometry and CRS preserved when df is sf) with the census columns added; a climasus_df with sus_meta stage = "census", type = <dataset>, same system, and a history entry. Rows are kept (left join); municipalities without census data get NA.

Details

Integration with censobr: wraps censobr::read_population(), read_households(), read_families(), read_mortality(), read_emigration() and read_tracts(), reading Arrow/Parquet data lazily, filtering to the municipalities present in df before collecting, and caching downloads in cache_dir.

Municipality join (join_level = "muni"): the census table is aggregated per municipality with aggregation_fun over all numeric columns selected and left-joined to df through the 7-digit municipality code column code_muni_7, which sus_spatial_join() (level = "munic") creates. df must therefore contain code_muni_7; join_muni_col is currently accepted but not used by the code. Aggregated columns get the suffix _<aggregation_fun> (e.g. V0001_sum) when translate_columns or standardize_values is TRUE.

Tract join (join_level = "tract"): if df is not a climasus_df (e.g. a plain sf of tracts) it is promoted automatically. Only the municipalities present in df (first 7 digits of the tract code) are read from censobr. If census_vars = NULL, all census columns except the geographic/identification ones (code_*, name_*, situacao, area_km2) are added; code_tract is always the join key. Raw censobr column names are kept, with no aggregation and no suffix.

Geographic columns follow the geobr/censobr standard (code_muni, code_state, abbrev_state, name_state, code_region, name_region, code_weighting).

Spatial data: if df is an sf object its geometry and CRS are preserved.

References

Pereira, Rafael H. M.; Barbosa, Rogerio J. (2023) censobr: Download Data from Brazil’s Population Census. R package version v0.4.0, https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=censobr. DOI: 10.32614/CRAN.package.censobr.

See also

sus_spatial_join(), sus_census_select(), sus_socio_compute_indicators(), sus_socio_list_indicators()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(climasus4r)

# Prepare spatial health data
sf_sim <- sus_data_import(uf = "SP", year = 2023, system = "SIM-DO") %>%
  sus_data_standardize(lang = "pt") %>%
  sus_spatial_join(level = "munic", lang = "pt")

# Add census population data
sf_enriched <- sus_census_join(
  df = sf_sim,
  dataset = "population",
  census_vars = c("V0001", "V0002"),
  year = 2010,
  lang = "pt"
)

# Join 2022 tract-level variables to an sf of setores (no aggregation)
setores <- geobr::read_census_tract(code_tract = 1100205, year = 2022)
setores <- sus_census_join(
  df = setores,
  dataset = "tracts",
  tracts_dataset = "Domicilio",
  year = 2022,
  join_level = "tract",
  join_tract_col = "code_tract",
  census_vars = c("V00001", "V00002"),
  lang = "pt"
)
} # }
